why: The product runs over every integer degree 1 to 179, so it contains the factor cos 90 = 0; the whole product is therefore 0.
Common denominator: [tan^2 A + (1+sec A)^2] / [tan A (1+sec A)]. Numerator = (sec^2 A - 1) + 1 + 2 sec A + sec^2 A = 2 sec A (sec A + 1), so the expression is 2 sec A / tan A = 2/sin A = 2 cosec A.
25c^2 + 5c - 12 = 0 gives c = 3/5 or -4/5. The constraint pi/2 < alpha < pi forces cos alpha = -4/5, hence sin alpha = +3/5, so sin 2alpha = 2(3/5)(-4/5) = -24/25.
At theta = 60, tan theta = sqrt 3, so (1 + 3) / (2 sqrt 3) = 4 / (2 sqrt 3) = 2/sqrt 3.
sec^2 - tan^2 = 1 gives (m+n)(m-n) = 1, so 1/(m+n) = m-n. The brace is (m+n)+(m-n) = 2m, and (1/m)(2m) = 2.
cosec + cot = 5/2 and (cosec - cot) = 1/(cosec + cot) = 2/5. Subtracting gives 2 cot = 5/2 - 2/5 = 21/10, so cot = 21/20 and tan = 20/21.
sin^2/(1+cos) = 1-cos, so the first two terms give 1-(1-cos) = cos. Also sin/(1-cos) = (1+cos)/sin, so the third and fourth terms cancel exactly. Total = cos theta.
cosec - cot = q implies cosec + cot = 1/q. Subtracting: 2 cot = 1/q - q = (1-q^2)/q, so cot = (1-q^2)/(2q).
The cotangents are 1/sqrt3, 1, sqrt3. Differences 0.4226 and 0.7321 are unequal so not an A.P., but each successive ratio is sqrt 3, so they are in G.P.
tan k . tan(90-k) = 1 pairs 1..44 with 89..46, and the unpaired middle factor is tan 45 = 1, so the product is 1.
